findings.title: [P2] Successful recovery leaves its failure alert visible
findings.rationale: web-app/src/telas/Inbox.tsx:179 sets the recovery failure alert, but neither executarRecuperacao's successful completion nor iniciarRodadaAutorizada at :223 clears it. The new regression at web-app/e2e/timeline.spec.ts:299 provides a concrete counterexample: abort three recovery responses, observe the error, then use Continue until complete ordered IDs are recovered and the pending banner disappears. The implementation still renders 'Não foi possível atualizar o histórico. Tente novamente.' after completion, while the recovery retry button has disappeared. Only another operation that independently clears erro removes this obsolete failure. The regression asserts the initial alert and final IDs/unread, but omits the final absence of that alert. This is exposed by the current recovery-error locus and newly delivered retry evidence; it does not reopen the resolved generation-protection finding. The frozen contract requires correct, visible and operable recovery/failure/retry states, so this remains a focused delivery correction in the current TODO.
findings.suggested_action: A, recommended: clear the error owned by the current recovery when that recovery completes successfully, preserving generation checks and any newer unrelated error. B: clear the recovery error when an authorized retry starts and restore it if that retry fails. C: retain the obsolete alert, leaving the recovery-state defect unresolved. Extend the existing real-network regression to require both pending-state removal and recovery-alert removal after successful coverage. Refresh affected Web validation and source-bound evidence; no architecture redesign or renewed product approval is needed.
